newsitem.title: USA: Florida insurance commissioner denies rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Florida insurance commissioner denies rate rise.

text.p: Florida's insurance commissioner on Wednesday denied a request by the state-run insurance pool to boost premiums on homeowners' policies, saying the request included an increase of more than 50 percent for mobile homes in hurricane-prone counties.

The Residential Property and Casualty Joint Underwriting Association (JUA), set up after Hurricane Andrew caused $16 billion in damage to South Florida in 1992, had requested a statewide increase of 5.3 percent for site built homes.
The JUA also called for average increases of 23 percent for mobile home owners, including rises of up to 56 percent for mobile home owners living in coastal counties.
Speaking from Tallahassee, Commissioner Bill Nelson called the rate rises "unfair and unjustifiable" and vowed to look for more equitable alternatives.

Ron Bartlett, spokesman for the JUA, said the association had not decided if it would file an amended rate proposal. The JUA also has questions about whether or not higher proposed deductibles were also rejected by Nelson. The state JUA covers 700,000 homeowners who could not get insurance from private carriers after Andrew. The industry-funded pool is Florida's second largest property insurer after State Farm Insurance.
